svg.text: Ghana: the 7 Acts every nurse must know

g.text: Act 857 (2013) — Health Professions Regulatory Bodies: YOUR licence
NMC registers, licenses, disciplines; practising unregistered/expired = offence;
obey Code + CPD; tribunal strikes off (Module 03's ladder lives here).
Act 846 (2012) — Mental Health: detention has rules
Voluntary vs involuntary admission (2 doctors + tribunal review); restraint last
resort, prescribed + time-limited + reviewed; patient rights + visitors protected.
Act 560 (1998) — Children's Act + Act 732 (2007) — Domestic Violence: REPORT
Abuse/neglect/defilement/trafficking → DOVVSU + Social Welfare + document injuries
(body map, quotes); consent for treatment shifts to protection — never mediate away.
Act 720 (2006) — Whistleblower: raising concerns is PROTECTED
Report danger/corruption internally (in-charge → management → NMC/CHRAJ) or to
prescribed bodies; victimisation-dismissal-demotion-transfer is unlawful; keep
copies + dates; media LAST (Module 6.2 ladder). Silence that harms = complicity.
Act 843 (2012) — Data Protection: health data is SENSITIVE
Process lawfully + minimally + securely; breach → notify Commission + subjects;
fines + prosecution attach — Module 04's locks are statutory, not courtesy.
Criminal Offences Act (1960) + Patients' Charter: bedside crimes + rights
Assault/battery (touch without consent), unlawful abortion outside legal grounds,
abandonment; Charter = dignity, info, consent, privacy, complaints (Module 04).
Deaths + police cases: special handling
Unnatural/sudden/unexplained/operative/maternal/custody deaths → DOCTOR certifies
cause; coroner-ordered post-mortems need NO family consent (explain kindly);
police cases (assault, RTA, poisoning, DOVVSU): preserve evidence (clothes bagged
+ labelled + handed with receipt), document verbatim, statements via in-charge —
treat first, but never wash away the case.
